passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2016, Seattle public high schools moved their start time from 7:50 a.m. to 8:45 a.m.
• Researchers measured students' sleep with wrist monitors before and after the change.
• After the change, students slept a median of 34 minutes more per night.
• Students' median biology grades rose by 4.5 percent.
stem: The student wants to emphasize the effect of the later start time on students' sleep. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: After Seattle high schools moved their start time from 7:50 a.m. to 8:45 a.m., students slept a median of 34 minutes more per night.
In 2016, Seattle public high schools moved their start time from 7:50 a.m. to 8:45 a.m., a change of almost an hour later in the morning.
After Seattle high schools started later in the morning, students' median biology grades rose by 4.5 percent compared with the year before.
To study the later start time, researchers used wrist monitors to measure the sleep of Seattle high school students before and after the change.
explanation: The goal is the effect on sleep. A names the change and the measured sleep gain. C is about grades, not sleep.
source: Emir original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
steps: The goal is the effect of the later start time on sleep.
The sentence needs both the change and the measured sleep result.
Only the choice reporting "a median of 34 minutes more per night" gives the effect on sleep.
The others give the change without its effect, the effect on grades, or the research method.
key: Rhetorical Synthesis: match the goal word for word. Here the goal is the effect on sleep.
